newsitem.title: UK: Guinness disputes LVMH plan for ventures.
newsitem.headline: Guinness disputes LVMH plan for ventures.

text.p: Britain's Guinness Plc, countering an attack by shareholder LVMH, said on Wednesday its position in the companies' joint ventures would be unaffected by its plan to merge with Grand Metropolitan Plc.
The statement came after LVMH said the merger would trigger a "control event" that would enable it to buy Guinness' interests in all the companies' joint ventures.

"Guinness is confident that a 'control event' will not be triggered by the completion of the proposed merger, and that there is therefore no basis for the assertion made by LVMH," the British drinks group said in a statement.
Guinness added that its 34 percent stake in LVMH's Moet Hennessy and its rights and obligations under the companies' various joint venture agreements would be unaffected by the merger.
"Guinness will continue to explore opportunities for further cooperation with Moet Hennessy," the firm said.
Earlier, LVMH reiterated its opposition to the merger, which would create GMG Brands, a food and drinks giant worth more than 20 billion pounds ($32.6 billion).

By buying Guinness' stakes in their joint ventures, the French drinks group said it would have the right under existing agreements to market and distribute Guinness brands in key markets such as China, Japan, France and the U.S. for at least 10 years.
Guinness' shares fell by 15 pence to 581, while GrandMet shed 15.5 pence to trade at 581 by 0955 GMT.
LVMH, which held a 14.2 percent stake in Guinness, has argued that it does not believe the Guinness-GrandMet deal would maximise shareholder value.
But Guinness and GrandMet have countered by saying that they have a range of highly complementary brands with few overlapping products. ($ = 0.613 British Pounds)
